newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa's condition better, doctors say.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa's condition better, doctors say.

text.p: The condition of Mother Teresa, recovering from heart surgery and pneumonia, improved on Wednesday, a regular medical update by her doctors said.

"Mother Teresa is better today. She had a good sleep last night. She had her morning tea around 0730 and morning prayer at 0815 hrs," said the medical bulletin issued at 8:30 a.m. (0300 GMT) by Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre.

Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda visited the 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun, winner of the 1979 Nobel peace prize, at the hospital on Tuesday and offered her a bouquet of roses with wishes for a speedy recovery.

The nun, known as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her work with the poor, was fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989. She had surgery last month to unblock two coronary arteries, the third such operation in five years.

But her recovery has been complicated by an irregular heartbeat, as well as lung and kidney problems. The heartbeat was corrected with a mild electric shock, but her bronchitis continued to cause concern to doctors.
Doctors have said they hope she can return home for Christmas, but have warned that her recovery would be slow.
